clauses.reason: This clause, the whole of Executive Order 11138, terminated on 1986-02-25 when EO 12553 revoked the order by number. Mechanism: express revocation by a numbered list ("Revocation of Various Executive Orders"; "any amendments thereto, are revoked:"); the target is identified by this row: "11138 Modifying provisions for the transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations". The effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (alternative: publication on 1986-03-03). Whether the one-person waiver was exhausted earlier by its use is not established by held evidence and is disclosed as open, not claimed.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (29 FR 225) prints Executive Order 11138 as an order of the President (Lyndon B. Johnson) dated 1964-01-07; the number, subject and date agree with the census register row (subject: Modifying Executive Order No., as amended by Executive Order No. 10103, providing for the transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations). I read the whole clause and signature block. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers every operative sentence; I confirm it as complete. The one operative clause modifies Executive Order No. 9721 of May 10, 1946, as amended by Executive Order No. 10103 of February 1, 1950 (transfer of personnel to public international organizations): it waives, with respect to one named person, Frederick Strauss, the Section 1 limit on the period during which a transferred employee is treated as on leave of absence and the Section 3(a) limit on the time within which reemployment rights may be exercised, and provides that he is considered to have been on leave of absence from August 12, 1957 through September 16, 1962 for all rights and benefits under Executive Order 9721, as amended. Ending: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986, titled "Revocation of Various Executive Orders", orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" Its table lists this order by number and subject on one line: "11138 Modifying provisions for the transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations". EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become, except, notwithstanding, nothing in, provided that and saving, with no hit outside table subjects); it is headed as an order of February 25, 1986 and signed that day, so the date is read as 1986-02-25, the signing date. The alternative reading is the Federal Register publication date, 1986-03-03 (Monday, March 3, 1986, 51 FR 7237); no later date is supported by the text. The quoted source for the end is the enacting paragraph of EO 12553, which names no order; the order is named by its row in the No./Subject table, quoted above, so the table row and the enacting paragraph are read together. This is a one-person waiver. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-28, a waiver exhausted by performance is recorded as such only where evidence shows it was used; no held source shows whether or when Mr. Strauss exercised reemployment rights or otherwise used the waiver, so no exhaustion date or interval is claimed and the question is disclosed as open. The waiver's surviving consequence (his deemed leave status and any rights that accrued) is distinct from the permission itself. The express revocation is the first ending shown by held evidence. Savings: EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception; rights that accrued to the named person before the revocation are treated as accrued, not as a continuing independent command. Searches selected after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): U.S. Code release point 119-121 (no hit for this order), eCFR as of 2026-10-14 (no hit), and the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (2 machine hits, the revocation note on this order and the matching note on EO 12553).
